emu_status.description: Execution state, CS:EIP (symbol-annotated), CPU mode, display state (scrn_xmax/ymax, text_disp, grph_disp) and fault_generation (non-zero once the core has faulted).

emu_prof_start.description: Start guest profiling (clears counters). Counts the instructions that trap in V86 mode on a 386 and every I/O access per port.

emu_prof.description: Guest profile: per-class counts and rates for INT/IRET/CLI/STI/PUSHF/POPF (the V86 #GP sources at IOPL<3), plus I/O totals and the busiest ports -- the ports that must be passed through via the TSS I/O permission bitmap.

emu_fault.description: Latest unrecoverable core fault (triple fault etc.): reason text with full register dump, CS:EIP, and a generation counter. The core freezes at the fault site, so emu_regs/emu_read_mem still show it until emu_resume.

emu_gdc.description: GDC / mode F/F / CRTC state: mode1 (68h), mode2 (6Ah), display and access page (A4h/A6h), display enable, GRCG, CRTC, and the uPD7220 parameter RAM (SYNC/CSRFORM/SCROLL/PITCH) for both GDCs. All of these are write-only or unreadable from the guest, so this is the only way to compare 'what mode is the machine in' between two runs.

emu_pic.description: 8259A master/slave IMR/ISR/IRR/ICW. The mask register is write-only from the guest, so this is the only way to see which interrupts a machine is actually set up to take -- use it to check what mask a real BIOS leaves behind before handing a guest to a V86 monitor.

emu_sound.description: Audio output level and FM/SSG state: peak of the mixed output since the last call (0 = silence, regardless of synthesizer), key-on bitmask and key-on register, the full OPN register file, and the SSG mixer/volumes. Use this instead of I/O port counts to tell 'the guest is writing to the chip' from 'sound is coming out'.

emu_regs.description: All CPU registers, segment bases, CR0-4, GDTR/IDTR; EIP annotated with symbol+offset.

emu_tvram.description: Text VRAM as UTF-8 (the on-screen text; screenshot replacement).

addr.description: hex address or kernel.map symbol (e.g. exec_run, timer_handler+0x10, 0x100000)
hex address or kernel.map symbol (e.g. exec_run, timer_handler+0x10, 0x100000)

emu_put_file.description: Place a host file at an arbitrary path inside the RUNNING guest, without a reboot or an NHD rewrite. Use this instead of the HostDrv+hsync round trip. guest_path may be omitted for a file the deploy manifests already know (e.g. apps/x/x.bin).

guest_path.description: absolute path in the guest, e.g. /usr/bin/x.bin

emu_deploy_status.description: State of the guest-side file-placement agent (present? staging window? last request).

emu_disasm.description: Disassemble n instructions of live guest memory via host objdump, with kernel.map symbols on labels and branch targets. Defaults to the current EIP.

addr.description: hex address or kernel.map symbol (e.g. exec_run, timer_handler+0x10, 0x100000)

emu_cmd.description: Run a shell command in the OS32 rshell over the embedded serial bridge; returns its output.

emu_key.description: Inject PC-98 keys. seq is comma-separated chords (SHIFT+SPACE,A,ENTER); text is literal ASCII.

emu_resume.description: Resume from a pause or a breakpoint.

emu_break_add.description: Set a breakpoint at an address/symbol.

addr.description: hex address or kernel.map symbol (e.g. exec_run, timer_handler+0x10, 0x100000)
hex address or kernel.map symbol (e.g. exec_run, timer_handler+0x10, 0x100000)

emu_step.description: Single-step n instructions; returns the new EIP. Requires a breakpoint (trap) pause -- emu_pause alone is not enough, so set a breakpoint and wait for trap_pause=1 first.

emu_trace.description: CS:EIP execution trace, symbol-annotated, one entry per line. Returns the tail by default and collapses repeated addresses to 'xN'.

emu_state_save.description: Save emulator state to a file (Windows path). Sends the aidebug token from np21w_aidebug_<port>.token.

emu_state_load.description: Load emulator state from a file.

emu_screenshot.description: Capture the screen to a BMP on the host filesystem (prefer emu_tvram for text screens).

path.description: output BMP path; default: a temp file
